answer: Identities post a claim-collateral bond into the hollow before settlement. The bond is 20 percent of claimed output, checked on the public lagoon ledger and locked to one record binding claim to key. A 500 claim costs 100; 1,000 fakes at 500 each post 100,000, the k-th paying the same 100, so splitting buys no discount. Auditors reject under-bonded claims; a false claim burns its bond. Claim inflation fails since bigger claims need bigger bonds; bond reuse fails since one record covers one claim. Verified claims reach the oasis pool; an honest agent posts 100 once and recovers it in full.
